title: ATAN2: 18 of 18 counted rows on the y/x-overflow error boundary, build 20026
status_plain: A real per-surface count with the Excel build restated on the same line. What was counted is Excel's error-placement boundary -- #NUM! exactly when x is non-zero and the implicit ratio y/x overflows -- not the bits of the returned angle. The source's own wording for those 18 rows is an exactness claim, which is why it is carried on the numeric axis under the convention that the math-deviation catalogue is a numeric register; the reader warning states what was actually measured.

counts.build_note: Restated on the same line as the figure.
counts.ambiguity_note: Axis is genuinely unresolved. The count measures an error-placement boundary, which is structural in shape, but the source's own wording is an exactness claim and the catalogue is a numeric register by convention. Published on the numeric axis with the boundary caveat rather than moved silently.
counts.source_sentence: - **Evidence:** live Excel 16.0 build 20026 (18/18 bit-exact); BUG-FUNC-027 B3, commit `8dea9cd`. Confidence **high**.

substrate: Excel forms the y/x ratio first; the division overflows and publishes #NUM!
open_question: No numeric-exactness count for the ATAN2 angle exists anywhere in OxFunc.
reader_warning: The boundary, not the angle, was measured. This count says nothing about the bits of any ATAN2 result that is not an error.
